findings.passage: It should be one citizen, one vote.
findings.note: From his press release urging the Senate to pass House Bill 4765, which the release says would require proof of U.S. citizenship to register and ID to cast a ballot.

findings.passage: Unfortunately, we have the worst secretary of state in America right here in Michigan, and we know noncitizens are finding their way onto our voter rolls, compromising the integrity of our free and fair elections.
findings.note: Same release; he links non-citizens on voter rolls to the case for the citizenship and ID bill and asks the Senate to act.

findings.passage: “This is exactly why I requested that the Justice Department monitor Michigan’s 2026 elections. Jocelyn Benson cannot be trusted to do her most basic job,” Nesbitt said.
findings.note: Same release; he cites non-citizen voting as the reason he asked for federal monitoring of the 2026 elections.

findings.passage: “We are blessed to have their leadership in a state where illegal immigrants have obtained driver’s licenses and a Chinese national was among at least 16 noncitizens who were confirmed to have cast ballots in our last general election.”
findings.note: Statement welcoming U.S. Justice Department efforts to compel voter-roll clean-ups in many states; he points to non-citizen ballots in the 2024 election. The opening of the quote names the federal officials leading the effort.

findings.passage: “Jocelyn Benson proves over and over again that she is the worst secretary of state in America and cannot be trusted with our voter rolls,” Nesbitt said.
findings.note: Same release; on keeping voter rolls accurate (the release cites 25,000 deceased people on the rolls).

findings.passage: It would be naive to assume this incident is the only instance of a noncitizen taking advantage of our state’s lax election laws.
findings.note: Statement after the report that a foreign national's ballot in Ann Arbor would be counted; he calls for answers from election officials.

findings.passage: They must assure the people of Michigan that there is more safeguarding the security of our elections than simply hoping criminals will turn themselves in.
findings.note: Same statement; he asks for safeguards beyond voters reporting themselves. No specific ID or citizenship-proof rule is named in it.

findings.passage: “From issuing driver’s licenses for illegal immigrants to Chinese nationals voting in our elections, all signs lead to the same conclusion: Jocelyn Benson is the worst secretary of state in American history and cannot be trusted to manage our elections,” said Nesbitt, R-Porter Township.
findings.note: Release on his letter, signed with 21 other legislators, asking the U.S. Justice Department to oversee Michigan's 2026 primary and general elections; the letter lists non-citizen ballots and voter-roll upkeep among its concerns.

findings.passage: She continues to fight against transparency and accountability, refuses to remove dead people from our state’s voter rolls and is happy to let noncitizens vote in our elections.
findings.note: Statement backing federal monitoring of Michigan's 2026 elections; on voter rolls and non-citizen voting.

findings.passage: The people of Michigan deserve absolute, unshakable confidence that their votes are legally cast and accurately counted.
findings.note: Statement backing a U.S. Justice Department review of Wayne County 2024 ballots; general election-integrity and federal-oversight position. No ID or citizenship rule named.

findings.passage: “There has been a lot of concern surrounding the election.
findings.note: 2020 statement on House and Senate oversight committees seeking election records; general election-integrity statement, earlier in time than the rest.
